summary.one_liner: Cache-Lite is a small Kotlin library and study project that builds a cache framework step by step, from a plain map to LRU and expirable caches.
summary.what_it_does: The README walks through designing a simple cache in Kotlin. It defines a Cache interface with size, set (operator []), get, remove and clear operations. PerpetualCache implements it with a HashMap that never evicts entries. LRUCache wraps any Cache using the decorator pattern and keeps at most a minimal size (default 100), evicting the least recently used entry via LinkedHashMap. ExpirableCache clears the whole cache after a flush interval (default one minute), checked lazily on each operation rather than by a background thread. The README also mentions FIFOCache, SoftCache and WeakCache, and a typealias for a generic cache type. Maven coordinates are given for use in a project.
use_cases: learn how caching works by reading source code
study cache design patterns in Kotlin
add a simple in-memory LRU cache to a Kotlin project
time-based whole-cache expiration for a small app
reference implementation for a build-your-own-cache exercise
how_to_run: Add the Maven dependency io.github.kezhenxu94:cache-lite:${cache-lite.version} to your pom.xml
notable: Walkthrough-style design: each cache type is introduced as a step in the README
LRUCache and ExpirableCache are decorators that wrap any Cache via Kotlin delegation
Expiration is lazy: the cache is recycled before each operation instead of using a scheduled task
Includes FIFO, soft-reference and weak-reference cache variants per the README
caveats: Explicitly described as a study case, not a production caching framework
Expiration clears the entire cache at once, not individual entries
README does not give installation details beyond the Maven snippet
